title: Beyond Scarcity: When Encoder Adaptation Is Worthwhile
abstract: arXiv:2610.41213v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-tailed recognition often learns a shared representation before correcting the classifier for class imbalance. Once the classifier has been rebalanced, however, final accuracy does not reveal whether further encoder adaptation remains worthwhile. Standard imbalance benchmarks obscure this question because they jointly vary the number of distinct examples available to rare classes and the frequency with which those examples shape the representation. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework that separates unique support from representation allocation and estimates the incremental value of encoder updates through matched classifier-only and full-network continuations from a common corrected model. The framework combines stage-specific controls, multiple representation and adaptation objectives, whole-distribution metrics, and hierarchical inference over class assignments, support reconstructions, and optimization runs. translated_title: 超越稀缺性：编码器适配何时才值得
translated_abstract: 长尾识别通常先学习一个共享表征，然后再针对类别不平衡对分类器进行纠正。然而，一旦分类器被重新平衡，最终准确率并不能揭示进一步的编码器适配是否仍然值得。标准的不平衡基准测试掩盖了这一问题，因为它们同时改变了稀有类别可用的独特样本数量以及这些样本塑造表征的频率。我们引入了一个受控评估框架，将独特支持与表征分配分离开来，并通过从同一个纠正后的模型出发进行匹配的仅分类器延续与全网络延续，来估计编码器更新的增量价值。该框架结合了阶段特定的控制手段、多种表征与适配目标、全分布指标，以及对类别分配、支持重构和优化运行的层次化推断。
tldr: 该论文提出一个受控评估框架，将稀有类别的独特样本量与表征分配解耦，用于量化长尾识别中编码器适配相对于仅重新平衡分类器所能带来的增量价值。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a controlled evaluation framework that disentangles rare-class unique support from representation allocation to quantify when encoder adaptation provides incremental value beyond classifier rebalancing in long-tailed recognition.
